newsitem.title: ZAIRE: ZAIRE SAYS JOURNALISTS NEED NEW ACCREDITATION.
newsitem.headline: ZAIRE SAYS JOURNALISTS NEED NEW ACCREDITATION.

text.p: Information Minister Kin-Kiey Mulumba on Monday told all foreign journalists covering Zaire's civil war that their press accreditation had been cancelled and they must seek new permission by Wednesday.
"Any journalist who does not have a new accreditation by Wednesday will be out of the country," he told a briefing called for foreign journalists.

Mulumba, who has been deeply critical of reporting on the war, also announced the setting up of an "ethics committee" to monitor foreign reporting of the conflict. He did not make clear if reports would be subject to checks before they left the country.

As the rebel drive to unseat President Mobutu Sese Seko has gained speed -- they now control about half the country -- foreign journalists have poured into Kinshasa to witness what may be the final days of the veteran leader's more than three decades in power.

About 200 foreign journalists are believed to be in the Zairean capital and it is unlikely the slow-moving bureaucracy could process that many applications for accreditation by the Wednesday deadline.
Mulumba, who has complained of "unfair and exaggerated" reporting, accused journalists of helping the rebel offensive by announcing claims of victories without verification.
He also suggested it would be better if journalists permanently assigned to cover Zaire for foreign media were Zairean.
